questions.question: Which of the following best describes the "services" view of the Internet?
options: A collection of billions of interconnected devices and links.
An infrastructure that provides services to distributed applications.
A strict set of protocols governing router behavior.
A hierarchy of Tier-1 and regional ISPs.
questions.correctAnswer: An infrastructure that provides services to distributed applications.
questions.explanation: The "services" view defines the Internet as an infrastructure providing services (like Web, email) to distributed applications, as opposed to the "nuts and bolts" hardware view.

questions.question: What defines the format, order of messages sent and received, and actions taken upon message transmission?
questions.explanation: This is the exact definition of a network protocol provided in the lecture.

questions.question: Which access network technology utilizes existing dedicated telephone lines to connect to a central office?
questions.explanation: DSL uses existing dedicated copper telephone lines to connect to a DSLAM in the central office, unlike Cable which uses a shared coaxial network.

questions.question: In packet switching, what is the requirement that an entire packet must arrive at a router before it can be transmitted to the next link called?
questions.explanation: "Store-and-forward" dictates that a router must receive all bits of a packet before it can begin transmitting the first bit onto the outbound link.

questions.question: Which type of network reserves end-to-end resources (like bandwidth) exclusively for a "call" between source and destination?
questions.explanation: Circuit switching reserves end-to-end resources (like a dedicated physical line or a reserved time slot) for the duration of a call.

questions.question: The time required to push a packet's bits onto a link is known as:
questions.explanation: Transmission delay is the time needed to push (transmit) the packet's bits into the link.

questions.question: If a packet has a length of L bits and the link transmission rate is R bits/sec, what is the transmission delay?
questions.explanation: The formula for transmission delay is the length of the packet (L) divided by the link transmission rate (R).

questions.question: Which delay component spikes exponentially as traffic intensity approaches the link's capacity?
questions.explanation: As traffic intensity (La/R) approaches 1, the queueing delay grows exponentially as packets pile up in the buffer.

questions.question: The end-to-end throughput of a network path is primarily constrained by:
options: The fastest link on the path
The processing power of the receiving host
questions.explanation: The bottleneck link is the link on the end-to-end path that constrains the overall throughput (it acts as the weakest link).

questions.question: Injecting packets into a network with a fake source address is known as:
questions.explanation: IP spoofing involves an attacker sending packets with a false source IP address to hide their identity or impersonate another host.

questions.question: In the Internet Protocol Stack, the Transport layer processes data into units called:
questions.explanation: In the encapsulation process, the transport layer creates a "segment", whereas the network layer creates a "datagram".

questions.question: Which layer is responsible for the routing of datagrams from source to destination?
questions.explanation: The network layer handles the routing of datagrams from source to destination (using protocols like IP).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of unguided physical media?
questions.explanation: Wireless radio is an unguided medium because signals propagate freely through the air/space, unlike guided media which use a physical wire or core.

questions.question: What is the global action of determining the source-to-destination path taken by packets called?
questions.explanation: Routing is the global action of determining the path, while forwarding is the local action of moving a packet from an input port to an output port.

questions.question: As a message moves down the protocol stack, each layer adds its own specific header information. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is the process where each layer wraps the payload from the layer above with its own specific header.

questions.question: The Internet core is primarily a client-server architecture, while the network edge is a mesh of interconnected routers.
questions.explanation: It is the opposite. The edge contains the hosts (client-servers), while the network core is the mesh of interconnected routers.

questions.question: Cable Internet access uses a shared broadcast medium where bandwidth is shared among homes.
questions.explanation: Cable uses a shared distribution network where multiple homes share the bandwidth to the cable headend.

questions.question: A botnet is often used to execute Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks.
questions.explanation: Attackers often use a network of compromised hosts (a botnet) to overwhelm a target with bogus traffic in a DoS attack.

questions.question: Propagation delay is determined by the length of the packet and the bandwidth of the link.
questions.explanation: Propagation delay is determined by the physical distance and the propagation speed of the medium (d/s). Length/bandwidth (L/R) calculates transmission delay.

questions.question: Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) divides a link's capacity by allocating specific frequency bands to different connections.
questions.explanation: TDM divides time into slots. FDM (Frequency Division Multiplexing) divides the capacity into frequency bands.

questions.question: Packet switching is generally better for handling "bursty" data than circuit switching.
questions.explanation: Packet switching allows for resource sharing and handles unexpected/bursty traffic better than circuit switching, which leaves reserved resources idle when not in use.

questions.question: The OSI reference model contains exactly the same five layers as the standard Internet protocol stack.
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers. It includes Presentation and Session layers, which are missing from the 5-layer Internet protocol stack.

questions.question: Throughput can never exceed the capacity of the bottleneck link on a path.
questions.explanation: A flow's end-to-end throughput is dictated by the slowest link on the path (the bottleneck link).

questions.question: A "traceroute" program measures the delay from a source host to each router along the path to a destination.
questions.explanation: The traceroute program works by sending probes to measure the delay to each router along the path toward a destination.

questions.question: The physical layer is responsible for moving entire frames from one network element to an adjacent network element.
questions.explanation: The Link layer transfers frames between neighboring elements. The Physical layer is responsible for transferring the individual bits "on the wire."
